sections.overview: This Australian murid rodent is known as the central pebble-mound mouse.
sections.identification: It has a yellow-brown to rufous back with dark guard hairs and a pale underside.
sections.habitat: It inhabits rocky country, open woodland, valleys and grassland, especially stony ridges and plains.
sections.diet: Species-specific diet data were not found in the consulted accounts.
sections.behavior: It constructs burrows and pebble mounds near their entrances; several mice may share a mound system.
sections.reproduction: The consulted species accounts provide no reproductive details.
sections.ecology: Pebble mounds are a conspicuous sign of this species, but tracks and other signs can resemble those of other small mammals.
sections.conservation: The Mammal Diversity Database lists its global IUCN category as Least Concern.
